Description: Anyscale on Azure is a managed platform for distributed Python and Ray workloads deployed on Azure Kubernetes Service. It helps teams run and manage distributed processing and AI applications using Azure resources, and the offering is currently in preview.

Arize AI Observability and Evaluation is a partner offering for monitoring, evaluating, and troubleshooting AI and machine-learning applications. Its Azure integration can support quality analysis and operational visibility for deployed models and LLM applications.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Native Arize AI Cloud Service

Description: Microsoft Entra ID, formerly Azure Active Directory, provides identity, single sign-on, and access management for users, applications, and devices. This namespace relates to identity and access administration rather than a stand-alone compute service.

Azure Communication Services exposes APIs and SDKs to add voice, video, chat, SMS, and email communications to applications. Developers use it to build customer engagement and collaboration experiences without running their own communication infrastructure.

Azure Data Box is a physical data-transfer service for moving large datasets between on-premises locations and Azure. Microsoft ships encrypted transfer appliances when network uploads or downloads are impractical.

Azure Database Migration Service helps move databases to Azure with assessment and migration workflows. It supports selected online and offline migrations while helping reduce downtime and migration complexity.

Azure Digital Twins models physical environments using digital representations of assets and their relationships. It lets applications combine IoT data with graph-based models to monitor and analyze real-world systems.

Azure IoT Central provides a managed application platform for connecting, monitoring, and managing IoT devices. It reduces the work needed to create dashboards, device templates, and operational workflows.

Log Analytics workspaces store and query telemetry collected through Azure Monitor. They support Kusto queries, troubleshooting, alerting, and operational reporting across Azure and connected environments.

Azure Red Hat OpenShift is a jointly managed OpenShift platform for running containerized applications on Azure. It provides enterprise Kubernetes capabilities with integrated operations and support from Microsoft and Red Hat.

This provider supports management and registration functions used by the Azure Stack family of hybrid-cloud products. It helps connect supported on-premises Azure environments with Azure management and marketplace capabilities.

Azure Synapse Analytics combines enterprise data integration, SQL analytics, and Apache Spark workloads in shared workspaces. It supports analytics pipelines, large-scale data exploration, and business intelligence.

Bing Search APIs expose web search functionality for applications through programmable endpoints. Availability and product terms can change, so implementations should verify the current Microsoft Bing Search offering.

Azure AI Bot Service helps create, connect, and manage conversational bots across applications and channels. It works with bot development frameworks and Azure AI capabilities to build interactive agents.

Commvault ContentStore is associated with Commvault data protection and storage management offerings integrated into Azure. It is a partner service rather than a general-purpose first-party Azure storage product.

Dynamics 365 Customer Insights unifies customer profiles and supports audience analysis and customer engagement experiences. This resource provider relates to the Dynamics service's Azure-based provisioning and integration functions.

This namespace relates to managing or coordinating database fleets across multiple database resources. A distinct public-facing Azure product corresponding exactly to this provider could not be reliably established.

Dell PowerScale for Azure brings Dell managed scale-out file storage to Azure for large unstructured datasets. It supports hybrid data movement and high-throughput file workloads through the OneFS-based platform.

Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services such as domain join, LDAP, Kerberos, and NTLM. It lets legacy applications use domain capabilities without operating traditional domain controllers.

Dynatrace Observability provides a partner-based application monitoring and observability integration on Azure. It can correlate telemetry across applications, services, and infrastructure to aid troubleshooting.
Edge Ordering supports ordering and lifecycle workflows for eligible Azure edge hardware devices. It is a supporting management provider rather than a separately marketed Azure application service.
This provider is associated with experimentation and controlled tests within Microsoft cloud experiences. Its public product scope is not clearly documented as a separately purchasable Azure service.

GitHub.Network represents networking resources associated with a GitHub partner or integrated Azure offering. A stand-alone Azure service and authoritative feature overview for this exact namespace were not established.

Informatica Data Management on Azure offers partner tooling for data integration, quality, governance, and related workflows. It helps enterprises connect and manage data across cloud and on-premises systems.

LambdaTest HyperExecute is a partner test-execution platform for running automated software tests at scale. Azure marketplace provisioning can connect this offering to Azure billing and resource management.
Liftrbasic.Samplerp appears to be a publisher-specific sample or test resource provider. No independently documented Azure service or dependable public functional description was identified.

Azure Machine Learning is a platform for building, training, deploying, and governing machine-learning models. It provides compute, experiments, pipelines, registries, and managed inference endpoints.

Microsoft.SaaS manages software-as-a-service purchases and subscriptions provisioned through Azure Marketplace. It supports marketplace offer lifecycle and billing integration rather than one particular SaaS product.
Microsoft.Addons is a core Azure resource provider for selected platform add-on registrations or resources. It is not itself a separately marketed Azure service.

Microsoft Entra Connect Health monitors identity synchronization and hybrid identity infrastructure. It helps administrators investigate availability, configuration, and sign-in-related issues for connected identity systems.

Azure Advisor analyzes Azure resources and recommends improvements in cost, security, reliability, operational excellence, and performance. It helps administrators prioritize configuration changes using Azure environment signals.
Azure Analysis Services hosts enterprise tabular semantic models for business intelligence and analytical reporting. It supports reusable data models and query access from supported BI tools.
Azure API Management publishes, secures, observes, and governs APIs through a managed gateway and developer portal. It supports policies, API versioning, access controls, and backend integration.
Azure App Configuration centrally stores application configuration settings and feature flags. It helps distributed applications update settings independently from code deployment.

Microsoft.App is the control-plane provider for Azure Container Apps and related managed environments. Azure Container Apps runs containerized applications and jobs with event-driven scaling and less infrastructure management.

Microsoft.Authorization manages role-based access control, policy-related authorizations, and access restrictions for Azure resources. It underpins secure delegation and governance across subscriptions and resource groups.
Azure Automanage automates selected configuration and operations best practices for supported virtual machines. It is used to apply management baselines and reduce repetitive administration.
Azure Automation runs operational runbooks and supports configuration and update-management workflows. It helps automate repeatable administration across Azure and hybrid infrastructure.

This provider historically manages Azure Active Directory B2C tenant resources for customer-facing identity scenarios. Azure AD B2C and Microsoft Entra External ID are related but have distinct service lifecycles and feature sets.
Associated Azure Service: Microsoft Entra External ID / Azure AD B2C

Description: Azure API Center provides a centralized inventory of APIs and their metadata across an organization. It helps teams discover APIs and understand governance, ownership, and lifecycle information.
Azure Attestation verifies evidence about the trustworthiness of hardware-backed or trusted execution environments. It supports policy-based validation for confidential-computing workloads.

Azure Event Hubs is a managed high-throughput event ingestion and streaming service. Applications use it for telemetry pipelines, streaming analytics, and large volumes of device or application events.

Azure Compute Fleet provisions and coordinates large collections of Azure virtual-machine capacity using flexible size and pricing preferences. It helps scale compute workloads across spot and standard virtual machines.
Azure HPC Cache accelerated access to on-premises or Azure storage for high-performance computing workloads. It is a legacy service, so customers should check its retirement and migration guidance.

Azure Lab Services provided managed environments for educational and training labs with controlled virtual-machine access. The service has reached retirement, and customers should review replacement options.

Azure Large Instances provides dedicated infrastructure configurations for workloads that require specialized large-memory or bare-metal capabilities. This provider manages related infrastructure resources and deployment metadata.
Azure Monitor collects and analyzes metrics, logs, and traces across applications and infrastructure. It powers dashboards, alerts, troubleshooting, and observability workflows.

Azure Notification Hubs distributes mobile push notifications at scale using platform notification services. It supports targeting, device registration, and notifications across multiple mobile ecosystems.
Azure Relay lets applications securely expose on-premises services to clients without opening inbound firewall ports. It facilitates hybrid connections between applications across network boundaries.
Azure Service Bus provides durable enterprise messaging through queues and publish-subscribe topics. It helps decouple services and supports reliable asynchronous communication.
Azure Spring Apps offered managed hosting and operations for Java Spring applications. Its lifecycle and retirement status should be verified before selecting it for new workloads.
Azure Stream Analytics processes streaming data using SQL-like queries over events as they arrive. It is commonly used for real-time telemetry analysis, filtering, aggregation, and anomaly detection.

Azure BareMetal Infrastructure provides dedicated physical server resources for specialized enterprise workloads. These instances can support applications with performance, licensing, or platform requirements not met by standard virtual machines.
Azure Batch schedules and runs large-scale parallel or high-performance jobs on managed pools of Azure compute nodes. It handles task distribution, scaling, and job orchestration for batch workloads.
Microsoft.Billing manages Azure billing accounts, profiles, invoices, and billing-related administrative resources. It supports tracking contractual and payment arrangements for Azure consumption.
Microsoft.BillingBenefits manages billing savings constructs such as Azure savings plans where supported. It provides resources for purchasing and administering eligible consumption discounts.

Azure Blueprints packaged repeatable governance configurations such as policy assignments, role assignments, and resource templates. It is a legacy governance service and customers should review current Azure policy and template alternatives.
This provider manages Azure Redis cache offerings for low-latency data access. Applications use Redis-compatible in-memory caching to improve throughput and response times.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Managed Redis / Azure Cache for Redis

Description: Microsoft.Capacity provides Azure platform capacity-related management capabilities. It is mainly an infrastructure or control-plane namespace rather than a separate customer-facing product.
Microsoft.CertificateRegistration manages SSL/TLS certificate resources associated with Azure App Service. It helps provision and manage certificates for secure application domains.
Azure Chaos Studio supports controlled fault-injection experiments against Azure applications and infrastructure. It helps teams validate resilience and understand system behavior during disruptions.
Microsoft.CloudTest relates to cloud-hosted testing resources and internal or specialized test workflows. A general-availability Azure service matching this namespace could not be established.
Microsoft.CognitiveServices provisions Azure AI services such as language, vision, speech, and Azure OpenAI-related resources. These managed APIs add pretrained AI capabilities to applications.
Microsoft.Commerce supports billing, offer, and commerce operations used by Azure platform services. It is an underlying commercial control-plane component rather than a distinct application service.
Microsoft.Compute manages virtual machines, disks, scale sets, and related compute infrastructure. It enables on-demand deployment and lifecycle management of virtualized workloads.
Microsoft.ComputeLimit relates to compute limit controls and associated resource requests. Its purpose is capacity governance rather than hosting compute workloads directly.
Azure Container Instances runs containers on demand without requiring customers to manage servers or Kubernetes clusters. It supports short-lived jobs and simple containerized services.

Azure Kubernetes Service provides managed Kubernetes clusters for deploying and operating containerized applications. Microsoft manages key parts of the control plane while customers manage application workloads and selected cluster configuration.
Azure Container Registry stores and manages container images and OCI artifacts. It integrates with build, security, and deployment workflows for Azure container platforms.
Azure Custom Providers extends the Azure Resource Manager control plane with custom resource types and actions. It lets developers present external or custom services as Azure-managed resources.

Customer Lockbox lets customers review and approve certain Microsoft engineer requests to access customer data during support operations. It increases oversight for exceptional support-access scenarios.

Azure Data Factory orchestrates data movement and transformation across supported cloud and on-premises systems. It supports pipelines, scheduled integration workflows, and data-processing activities.
Microsoft.DataReplication manages resources related to replicating data between systems or locations. The exact publicly marketed product represented by this namespace is not clearly established.
Azure Data Share lets organizations share datasets across organizational boundaries with controlled access. It supports governed sharing scenarios without building bespoke data-transfer systems.

Azure Databricks provides an integrated Apache Spark-based environment for data engineering, analytics, and AI. It supports collaborative notebooks, pipelines, lakehouse architectures, and machine learning.

Azure Data Lake Analytics was a distributed analytics service that ran data-processing jobs against large datasets. It is a legacy offering; customers should check retirement guidance and newer analytics alternatives.

Microsoft.DataLakeStore historically managed Azure Data Lake Store accounts and related analytics storage resources. Data lake workloads now commonly use Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 built on Azure Blob Storage.
Azure Database for MariaDB was a managed MariaDB database hosting service. The offering has retired, and applications should use a supported database migration target.
Azure Database for MySQL provides managed MySQL hosting with automated maintenance, backup, and scaling options. It reduces operational effort for relational MySQL applications.

Azure Database for PostgreSQL offers managed PostgreSQL hosting with backups, high availability, and configurable compute. It supports relational application and analytics workloads without managing database servers directly.
Microsoft.DevHub supports developer-oriented Azure integration and deployment experiences. It appears to be a supporting provider rather than the namespace of one major standalone Azure product.

Microsoft.Devices is the resource provider for Azure IoT Hub and the IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service. It enables secure device connectivity, messaging, device management, and automated provisioning.
Azure DevTest Labs provides self-service virtual-machine environments with policies, reusable configurations, and cost controls. It is designed for development, testing, and training workflows.

Microsoft.DocumentDB manages Azure Cosmos DB database accounts and related database resources, as well as DocumentDB-related offerings. These services provide managed document and other database capabilities for applications.
Microsoft.DomainRegistration manages domain-registration resources for websites hosted using Azure App Service. It supports domain purchase and lifecycle integration with application hosting.

Microsoft.EnterpriseSupport represents Azure enterprise support-plan or support-related management functions. It is primarily an administrative provider rather than a separately deployed application service.
Azure Event Grid routes events from Azure services and custom publishers to subscribers. It supports event-driven applications using filtering, push delivery, and messaging integration.

Microsoft Fabric is a unified data and analytics SaaS platform spanning integration, engineering, warehousing, real-time analytics, and BI. This provider supports Fabric-related Azure resource management and integration.
Microsoft.Features manages registration of preview and other subscription-scoped Azure features. It is a core control-plane capability rather than a consumer-facing service.
Guest Configuration assesses or applies selected configurations inside virtual machines through Azure Policy. It helps audit operating-system and software settings across Azure and hybrid machines.
Azure Dedicated HSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for customer-controlled cryptographic operations. The service addresses specialized key custody and compliance scenarios.

Microsoft.HybridCompute manages Azure Arc-enabled server resources representing machines outside native Azure compute. It extends Azure inventory, policy, governance, and monitoring to hybrid servers.

Microsoft.InferenceService relates to managed model-inference capabilities on Azure. It supports deploying or using AI inference endpoints, although the exact public product scope of this provider may be specialized.

Microsoft.IoTSecurity covers IoT threat protection and security insights for connected devices and environments. It is associated with Microsoft Defender for IoT capabilities for identifying and managing device-related risks.
Azure Key Vault securely stores and controls access to secrets, certificates, and encryption keys. It helps applications and administrators manage sensitive credentials and cryptographic material.

Microsoft.KubernetesConfiguration manages extensions and configuration resources for Kubernetes clusters connected to Azure Arc. It supports declarative configuration and GitOps-style cluster management.
Azure Logic Apps automates workflows across services using triggers, actions, and prebuilt connectors. It is commonly used for systems integration, event processing, and business process automation.
Microsoft.Maintenance manages maintenance schedules and configuration for supported Azure infrastructure. It helps administrators coordinate platform updates within defined maintenance windows.

Managed identities provide Microsoft Entra identities to Azure workloads without requiring application-managed credentials. They enable access to supported services through token-based authentication.
Microsoft.ManagedServices enables Azure Lighthouse delegated resource management across tenants. Service providers use it to manage customer resources securely without switching tenant contexts.
Microsoft.Management manages management groups used to organize multiple Azure subscriptions in a hierarchy. This structure supports inheritance of governance policies and access controls at scale.

Microsoft.Marketplace supports discovery and administration of cloud marketplace products and offers. It is part of the Azure commercial marketplace infrastructure rather than one third-party product.
Microsoft.MarketplaceOrdering handles purchase terms and ordering for selected Azure Marketplace offers. It helps manage offer acceptance and acquisition in the Azure control plane.
Microsoft.Monitor is associated with Azure Monitor control-plane operations and monitoring resources. Azure Monitor collects metrics, logs, and traces to support alerting and operational analysis.

Microsoft.Intune is listed by Microsoft among Azure Monitor-related resource providers, despite the Intune branding of the namespace. Its Azure control-plane use should not be confused automatically with the full Microsoft Intune device-management product.

Microsoft.Network manages virtual networks, load balancers, gateways, firewalls, DNS, and numerous other networking resources. It provides connectivity, traffic control, and network security for Azure workloads.
Microsoft.OperationsManagement supports Azure monitoring and management solution resources. It has been used with Log Analytics workspaces and related operational insights features.
Microsoft.PolicyInsights provides compliance evaluations, policy state information, and policy event data for Azure Policy. It helps teams report on and investigate resource governance compliance.
Microsoft.Portal manages resources used by the Azure portal such as dashboards. It supports customer-facing management experiences rather than application hosting.
Microsoft.PowerBIDedicated provisions dedicated Power BI capacity resources in Azure. It supports embedding and serving Power BI reports and analytics in customer-facing applications.

Microsoft.PowerPlatform manages Azure-integrated resource types supporting Power Platform environments and services. Power Platform provides low-code apps, automation, analytics, and agent-building capabilities.

Microsoft Purview provides data governance, compliance, and information protection capabilities across data estates. Azure resources under this provider can support governance accounts and related services.
Azure Resource Graph enables fast queries over Azure resource metadata across subscriptions. It helps teams inventory, explore, and govern large numbers of resources using query expressions.

Microsoft.ResourceIntelligence appears to support specialized analysis or intelligence over Azure resource data. A separately marketed service and specific public documentation for this namespace could not be reliably determined.
Azure Resource Notifications publishes events when supported Azure resources or their states change. It allows automation and monitoring systems to react to control-plane or health-related updates.

Microsoft.ResourceConnector manages the Azure Arc resource bridge appliance used to project resources from supported private-cloud environments into Azure. It enables Azure-based management of selected on-premises virtualized infrastructure.
Azure Resource Health reports the availability and health state of individual Azure resources. It helps distinguish service incidents from resource-specific failures and supplies diagnostic context.

Microsoft.Resources is a core provider for Azure resource groups, deployments, template specifications, and related operations. It underpins consistent management of Azure resources through the control plane.
Microsoft.HanaOnAzure manages SAP HANA on Azure Large Instances resources and associated infrastructure. The offering supports specialized SAP database deployments requiring dedicated infrastructure.
Associated Azure Service: SAP HANA on Azure Large Instances

Description: Azure AI Search provides indexing and retrieval of structured and unstructured content for applications. It supports full-text, semantic, vector, and hybrid search scenarios.

Microsoft.Security exposes security assessments, recommendations, and posture-management resources associated with Defender for Cloud. The service helps identify threats and improve cloud workload security.

Microsoft.SecurityInsights is the primary resource provider for Microsoft Sentinel analytics and security operations resources. Sentinel ingests security data and supports detection, investigation, and response workflows.

Microsoft.SecurityDetonation is associated with examining suspicious content in isolated environments for security analysis. Its externally supported capabilities are not clearly described as a standalone Azure service.

Microsoft.ServiceNetworking manages networking-related services used to connect and expose applications. Its exact resource types should be checked before treating it as synonymous with one Azure networking product.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Application Gateway for Containers / service networking

Description: Azure Service Fabric is a distributed-systems platform for building and operating scalable microservices and applications. It provides orchestration, health monitoring, and lifecycle management for stateful and stateless services.
Azure Service Fabric Mesh was a managed container hosting offering built on Service Fabric. It is a legacy service and should not be selected without checking current availability and support.

Microsoft.Singularity is associated with specialized Microsoft compute orchestration or infrastructure systems. There is no clearly documented public Azure service that corresponds one-to-one with this namespace.

Microsoft.Sql manages Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and some related SQL analytics resources. These offerings provide managed relational database platforms for transactional and enterprise applications.
Azure Storage offers scalable cloud object, file, queue, and table storage through Azure storage accounts. It provides durable managed storage for applications, backups, and analytics.
Azure Storage Actions automates bulk data operations on Azure Blob Storage according to defined conditions and schedules. It reduces custom code needed for repetitive object-storage management.
Microsoft.Subscription provides operations for managing Azure subscriptions and subscription requests. It is a central platform resource provider used in organizational Azure administration.
Microsoft.Support supports creation and management of Azure support tickets and selected support plan operations. It connects Azure customers with Microsoft support workflows.
Microsoft.Web manages Azure App Service sites, web apps, functions, hosting plans, and related web resources. It enables managed hosting for web applications and serverless functions.
Microsoft.AlertsManagement manages alerts, alert processing rules, and related operational response resources. It helps centralize and control alerting across Azure Monitor.

Microsoft.AppAssessment is associated with discovery or assessment of applications ahead of cloud migration or modernization. Public documentation does not clearly establish it as a distinct customer-facing service.

Microsoft.AppComplianceAutomation supports compliance assessment and automated evidence or attestation workflows for applications. The provider is associated with Microsoft cloud compliance capabilities rather than general application hosting.

Microsoft.ApplicationMigration relates to migrating applications into Azure environments. It is best understood as a supporting migration capability rather than necessarily a separate product from Azure Migrate.
Microsoft.AppLink appears to provide application-linking or integration management resources. A distinct documented Azure service corresponding to this namespace could not be confirmed.

Microsoft.Approvals supports approval-related resources or workflows within Azure-integrated services. The public scope and product branding of this provider are not sufficiently clear to assert more specific capabilities.

Microsoft.ArcContainerStorage manages container storage resources associated with Azure Arc environments. It supports persistent storage scenarios for supported Kubernetes deployments outside ordinary Azure-hosted clusters.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Container Storage enabled by Azure Arc

Description: Azure VMware Solution hosts VMware private clouds on dedicated Azure infrastructure, including vSphere, vSAN, and NSX capabilities. It helps organizations migrate and operate VMware workloads while connecting them to native Azure services.

Microsoft.AWSConnector represents AWS environment connections used for cross-cloud discovery or management from Azure. It allows selected resources outside Azure to participate in Azure management workflows.

Azure Arc-enabled data services extend Azure database management experiences into Kubernetes-based hybrid environments. This provider manages Arc data controllers and related connected data-service resources.

Microsoft.AzureBusinessContinuity relates to Azure business continuity management across backup and disaster recovery workloads. Its resources help provide a centralized view of protection and resilience status.

Microsoft.AzureContextCache appears to support context caching for Azure platform or application capabilities. No dedicated public Azure product description for this namespace could be reliably identified.
Microsoft.AzureDataTransfer is associated with orchestrating managed data-transfer jobs or resources in Azure. The precise supported scenarios depend on the service version and resource types.

Microsoft.AzureImageTestingForLinux relates to automated testing of Linux images intended for Azure environments. It is a specialized validation provider rather than a general virtual-machine hosting service.

Microsoft Playwright Testing provided managed Playwright browser testing with parallel cloud execution and test result reporting. The service was retired on March 8, 2026, and Microsoft directs customers to Azure App Testing for replacement functionality.
Microsoft.AzureResilienceManagement is associated with assessing or managing cloud workload resilience. Its public, standalone product positioning is not clearly documented for this exact provider.
Microsoft.AzureScan appears to provide resource or workload scanning through an Azure platform control plane. No confirmed public product-level description was found for this provider.

Azure Sphere provides a secured IoT device platform combining a dedicated operating system, cloud security service, and supported microcontrollers. It is designed to protect internet-connected devices throughout their lifecycle.
Azure Local enables deployment and management of Azure-integrated infrastructure in customer data centers and edge sites. It supports virtualized workloads and hybrid management with Azure.

Microsoft.AzureTerraform relates to Terraform-based Azure infrastructure management capabilities. This provider is not itself the Terraform tool and is not clearly documented as a separate commercial service.
Microsoft.BareMetal manages specialized Azure bare-metal resource types and infrastructure. It supports scenarios where dedicated physical hosts are required instead of ordinary virtual machines.
Microsoft.BillingTrust appears to represent internal or specialized billing-assurance capabilities. Its exact functionality is not documented as an independently marketed Azure service.
Microsoft.BlockchainTokens was associated with Azure blockchain token-related resources. It is a legacy namespace and may no longer correspond to an available production service.
Microsoft.Carbon is associated with cloud carbon or emissions-related resources. Related reporting capabilities help organizations understand or report environmental impact from cloud consumption.

Microsoft.Cdn manages Azure content delivery and edge-acceleration resources, including Front Door-related capabilities. These services cache and route web content closer to users to improve availability and performance.

Microsoft.ChangeSafety supports risk-reduction and safety checks around Azure service deployment changes. Microsoft identifies it as a core platform provider rather than a product customers deploy directly.
Microsoft.CleanRoom relates to controlled data collaboration using isolated or governed environments. The precise product and data-sharing guarantees should be verified for the deployed offering.

Microsoft.CloudDevicePlatform represents a supporting platform for device-oriented management or integration capabilities. A distinct, broadly documented Azure product for this exact namespace has not been confirmed.

Microsoft.CloudHealth manages health models that combine monitored entities, relationships, and signals. These resources can express application health in terms of related components and their telemetry.

Azure Artifact Signing is a managed software-signing service that handles certificate lifecycle and secure signing operations. It helps software publishers establish trust in distributed applications and integrate signing into build pipelines.

Microsoft.ComputeSchedule provides resource operations for scheduling selected virtual-machine or compute activities. It supports automation of time-based compute operations rather than a distinct machine-hosting platform.

Azure Confidential Ledger provides an append-only tamper-evident data store protected by confidential-computing technologies. It is intended for high-integrity audit trails and records that need verifiable integrity.
Microsoft.Confluent provisions and manages an integrated Confluent Cloud partner offering on Azure. Confluent supports managed Apache Kafka-based data streaming and event-driven applications.
Microsoft Connected Cache enables distributed content caching to reduce bandwidth use when delivering supported Microsoft content. Azure resources may manage connected cache nodes and deployments.
Microsoft.ConnectedCredentials appears to support credential exchange or management for connected infrastructure. Its exact relationship to customer-facing Azure products is not clearly documented.

Microsoft.ConnectedOpenStack manages connections to supported OpenStack environments through Azure Arc capabilities. It is used to represent or manage eligible off-Azure virtualization resources through Azure.
Microsoft.ConnectedVehicle appears to support connected-vehicle platform resources and integrations. A discrete public Azure service definition for this namespace could not be reliably established.

Azure Arc-enabled VMware vSphere brings on-premises VMware inventories and selected virtual-machine management actions into Azure. It helps apply Azure management and governance capabilities to VMware infrastructure.
Microsoft.Consumption provides usage, reservations, budgets, and consumption-related data or controls for Azure costs. It underpins cost visibility and spending governance across Azure subscriptions.
Microsoft.CostManagement provides cost analysis, forecasting, budgets, and optimization management features. It helps organizations understand and control their Azure cloud spending.
Microsoft.CostManagementExports configures scheduled exports of cloud cost and usage data to storage. This helps organizations build external reporting, finance, and chargeback pipelines.
Microsoft.Dashboard is associated with Azure Managed Grafana dashboard instances and management. Azure Managed Grafana provides a managed Grafana environment for dashboards and observability.

Azure SQL Database Watcher provides monitoring for Azure SQL workloads using a managed data collection and analysis experience. It helps database teams inspect performance and investigate SQL resource issues.
Microsoft.DataBoxEdge manages Azure Stack Edge devices that provide Azure-connected compute and data processing at edge locations. It supports local processing and transfer of data to Azure services.

Microsoft.Datadog provisions and integrates Datadog monitoring through Azure Native Integrations. It helps collect and analyze infrastructure and application telemetry within a partner observability service.
Microsoft.DataProtection manages modern backup policies, vaults, and backup instances used with Azure Backup. It supports workload protection and recovery through centrally managed resources.

Microsoft.DependencyMap relates to discovery and visualization of application or infrastructure dependencies. These capabilities help operations teams understand connected components and service relationships.
Azure Virtual Desktop delivers managed virtual desktops and remote applications from Azure. It provides pooled or personal desktops with centralized user access and session-host management.

Microsoft.DevCenter manages development centers and projects for cloud-hosted developer workstations and environment provisioning. It supports developer self-service with governance and standardized images or infrastructure.
Associated Azure Service: Microsoft Dev Box / Azure Deployment Environments

Description: Microsoft.DevelopmentWindows365 is associated with Windows 365 development or Cloud PC resources. Windows 365 streams persistent Windows desktops from Microsoft-managed cloud infrastructure.
Microsoft.DeviceOnboarding supports device registration or onboarding workflows in Azure-connected environments. Its exact public product scope depends on the device platform using the provider.

Azure Device Registry provides centralized records and metadata for devices and assets in industrial and edge environments. It supports discovering and representing devices that participate in Azure IoT Operations.
Device Update for IoT Hub distributes and manages software and firmware updates for IoT devices. It helps operators stage deployments, track update progress, and manage device fleets.
Managed DevOps Pools provides Microsoft-managed agent pools for Azure DevOps pipelines. It helps teams run scalable build and release jobs without directly maintaining self-hosted VM agents.

Microsoft.Discovery is associated with discovery and inventory of resources or environments for Azure workflows. Public information is insufficient to identify a single stand-alone product for this namespace.

Microsoft.DurableTask provides managed orchestration infrastructure for durable, long-running application workflows. It coordinates task state and execution for applications using durable task patterns.

Microsoft.Easm is associated with discovery and monitoring of internet-exposed assets. External Attack Surface Management helps security teams understand externally reachable infrastructure and potential risks.
Associated Azure Service: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management

Description: Microsoft.Edge provides edge-site management resources associated with Azure Arc. Azure Arc site manager organizes and manages edge infrastructure at scale from Azure.

Microsoft.EdgeMarketPlace supports marketplace-style distribution or management of offerings for edge environments. It is an auxiliary resource provider rather than a generally marketed Azure marketplace product.
Microsoft.EdgeZones manages selected edge-zone connectivity and deployment resources. Azure edge locations can place compute or services closer to users and devices for latency-sensitive workloads.

Microsoft.Elastic provisions Elastic's managed search, logging, and observability platform through Azure Native Integrations. It streamlines deployment, single sign-on, and billing of the partner offering.
Entitlement management automates requests, approvals, assignments, and expiration of access packages. It helps organizations govern access to groups, applications, and SharePoint resources.

Microsoft Entra ID Governance helps manage identity lifecycles, access reviews, and privileged or entitlement access. This provider supports governance-related identity resources and provisioning workflows.

Microsoft.ExtendedLocation represents nonstandard deployment locations, such as Azure Arc-enabled custom locations. It lets supported Azure resource types be deployed or managed in connected environments.
Microsoft.FileShares supports file-sharing-related Azure resource types. For general-purpose SMB and NFS cloud file shares, the associated customer-facing product is Azure Files.

Azure Fluid Relay provides a managed service for synchronizing collaborative application state using the Fluid Framework. It supports real-time multiuser collaboration without developers building the synchronization backend.

Microsoft.GCPConnector represents resources for connecting Google Cloud environments with Azure management workflows. Its purpose is multicloud integration rather than hosting Google Cloud workloads in Azure.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Arc multicloud management (Google Cloud connector)

Description: Microsoft.Genome relates to genomic data or analysis infrastructure within the Azure ecosystem. The namespace is not clearly documented as one currently available public Azure genomics product.

Microsoft.GraphServices exposes Azure resources related to Microsoft Graph integration. These capabilities can help applications use Microsoft 365 organizational data and related APIs from Azure-managed resources.

Microsoft.Hardware represents specialized hardware-related resource management in Azure. It is an infrastructure-facing provider rather than an independently marketed general-purpose hardware service.

Azure HDInsight provides managed open-source analytics clusters, including supported Apache big-data technologies. It is used for large-scale data processing without building the underlying cluster infrastructure from scratch.

Azure AI Health Bot helps organizations create healthcare-oriented conversational experiences and virtual assistants. It includes healthcare-focused language and workflow capabilities for patient and administrative interactions.

Microsoft.HealthcareApis manages healthcare API and data workspace resources associated with Azure Health Data Services. These services enable standardized handling of clinical information using formats such as FHIR and DICOM.

Microsoft.HealthcareInterop provides resource types related to healthcare data interoperability and exchange. It supports capabilities in the broader Azure healthcare-data integration ecosystem, though its precise product branding may vary.
Microsoft.HealthDataAIServices represents healthcare-focused AI or data-processing resources. A fully defined public product mapping for this exact namespace has not been established.

Microsoft.Help provides help, diagnostics, and support-related operations through Azure management experiences. It assists users with troubleshooting and guided resolution rather than hosting applications.

Microsoft.HybridConnectivity enables connectivity scenarios for resources outside Azure managed through Azure Arc. It supports secure communication paths between Azure services and connected infrastructure.

Microsoft.HybridContainerService is associated with deploying or managing hybrid Kubernetes services through Azure. It supports connected container environments and their Azure management integrations.

Microsoft.HybridNetwork manages network-function resources for hybrid and operator networking deployments. It supports deploying and managing virtual or containerized network functions in eligible environments.

Microsoft.Impact records or evaluates customer workload impacts associated with Azure platform conditions. The resource provider is primarily used for operational or support workflows rather than a stand-alone product.

Microsoft.IntegrationSpaces relates to integration-space resource management for connecting systems and workflows. A definitive public product association for this exact namespace was not established.

Microsoft.Inventory manages inventory-related resource information or discovery workflows within Azure services. It should be treated as a supporting namespace unless a specific resource type identifies the product.
Microsoft.IoTFirmwareDefense supports analysis of firmware images for security weaknesses and risky components. It helps device manufacturers and operators assess embedded software security.
Associated Azure Service: Microsoft Defender for IoT firmware analysis

Description: Azure IoT Operations brings data ingestion, processing, and messaging capabilities to Azure Arc-enabled edge environments. It helps industrial applications connect local devices and move operational data to cloud services.
Microsoft.IoTOperationsDataProcessor manages data-processing resources associated with Azure IoT Operations. It supports transformation and routing of industrial or device data near the edge.

Microsoft.Kubernetes connects non-Azure Kubernetes clusters to Azure Arc for inventory and management. It extends Azure policy, extensions, and management capabilities to eligible Kubernetes distributions.

Microsoft.KubernetesRuntime supports Azure-managed Kubernetes runtime capabilities in connected or hybrid environments. It provides control-plane resources for selected edge or Arc-based orchestration scenarios.

Azure Data Explorer is a managed analytics service optimized for fast queries across large volumes of telemetry and event data. It uses Kusto Query Language for real-time operational and exploratory analytics.

Azure Load Testing runs cloud-based performance tests to assess how applications behave under load. It integrates with testing tools and Azure monitoring to help identify throughput or latency bottlenecks.

Microsoft.ManagedNetworkFabric provides resource management for network-fabric infrastructure used in Azure Operator Nexus environments. It supports controlled configuration of switching and connectivity in telecommunications clouds.

Microsoft.ManagedOps provides resources for creating and managing ManagedOps instances. Its customer-facing positioning is not clearly documented, so it should not be assumed to be a general Azure operations product.
Azure Maps provides geospatial APIs for maps, routing, geocoding, and location intelligence. Applications use it to add mapping and spatial services without running their own geospatial backend.
Microsoft.MessagingCatalog appears to manage catalogs or definitions of messaging-related resources. It is not clearly identified as a standalone Azure messaging service.
Microsoft.MessagingConnectors appears to support integration connectors for messaging workflows. Its exact publicly supported features and product association are not established.
Azure Migrate provides discovery, assessment, and migration tools for moving servers, databases, and applications to Azure. It helps plan cloud adoption and track modernization projects.
Microsoft.Mission represents mission-oriented cloud or specialized operations resources. The precise public offering associated with the namespace is not clearly defined.

Microsoft.MySQLDiscovery supports discovery or assessment of MySQL database environments for management or migration. It is a supporting database workflow provider rather than a replacement for Azure Database for MySQL.

Azure NetApp Files provides enterprise-grade managed file storage with SMB and NFS protocol support. It is designed for applications that need high throughput, low latency, and predictable storage performance.
Microsoft.NetworkCloud manages network-cloud resources for Azure Operator Nexus. Azure Operator Nexus supports carrier-grade cloud infrastructure and workloads in telecommunications environments.

Microsoft.NetworkSecurity exposes specialized cloud-network security resources and policies. It relates to protecting traffic and access in Azure networking, but the exact feature set depends on the resource type.

Microsoft.NexusIdentity manages identity-related resources associated with Azure Operator Nexus. It supports security integration for operator cloud infrastructure rather than a general directory service.

Microsoft.Nutanix relates to the deployment and integration of Nutanix workloads or managed offerings on Azure. It enables enterprises to extend familiar Nutanix virtualization operations into Azure infrastructure.
Microsoft.OffAzure represents machines or discovered resources outside Azure during migration assessment. It helps Azure Migrate inventory and evaluate external infrastructure before migration.

Microsoft.OnlineExperimentation is associated with controlled online experiments, such as feature comparisons and measurement of outcomes. A single generally available product matching this resource provider has not been established.

Microsoft.OpenEnergyPlatform relates to cloud-based energy data platforms or open energy data workflows. It is a specialized industry provider and should not be assumed to be a general-purpose Azure analytics service.
Microsoft.OperatorVoicemail relates to voicemail-related services for operator or telecom scenarios. The public product capabilities of this provider are not clearly documented.
Azure Orbital provides cloud-integrated satellite communications and ground-station-related capabilities. It is designed to help space organizations process and connect satellite data using Azure.

Azure Peering Service improves connectivity between customer networks and Microsoft services through direct and optimized peering relationships. It supports predictable network routing and connectivity performance.
Microsoft.Pki is associated with public-key infrastructure and certificate management capabilities. Its precise relationship to managed certificate offerings depends on the resource types being used.
Microsoft.PlatformValidation supports validation of platform configurations or deployments. This is a supporting provider and not a clearly documented customer-facing Azure service.
Microsoft.PortalServices manages supporting services and resources used in Azure portal experiences. It is not a separate service for deploying customer application workloads.
Microsoft.PowerBI represents Power BI-related Azure management resources. Power BI provides interactive reporting, semantic models, and dashboards for analyzing business information.
Microsoft.ProgramEnrollment supports enrollment or eligibility management for selected Microsoft cloud programs. It is an administrative provider rather than a workload hosting service.

Microsoft.ProviderHub manages provider registration or development infrastructure for Azure Resource Manager resource providers. It serves platform extensibility and provider-lifecycle scenarios rather than typical application workloads.
Azure Quantum provides a cloud platform for quantum-computing tools, resources, and partner hardware access. It supports quantum development and selected optimization and research workflows.
Microsoft.Quota provides APIs for reviewing and requesting quota increases for supported Azure resource types. It helps teams manage service capacity limits before deploying or scaling workloads.

Microsoft.RecoveryServices manages recovery services vaults used for data backup and disaster-recovery scenarios. It supports retention, recovery points, and replication configuration for protected workloads.
Microsoft.Relationships represents relationship metadata or connections among certain managed Azure resources. No single standalone Azure service can be confidently associated with the namespace.

Microsoft.ResourceBuilder relates to construction or authoring workflows for Azure resource definitions. Its public feature scope is not documented sufficiently to claim a separately marketed product.
Microsoft.SaaSHub supports central experiences or operations for SaaS solutions subscribed to through Azure Marketplace. It is part of the broader commercial marketplace ecosystem.

Azure Monitor SCOM Managed Instance provided a cloud-managed alternative for selected System Center Operations Manager monitoring scenarios. Microsoft deprecated it in September 2025 and recommends migrating to supported SCOM or Azure Monitor options.
Microsoft.SCVMM connects System Center Virtual Machine Manager infrastructure to Azure Arc. It enables Azure inventory and selected management operations for virtual machines managed by SCVMM.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Arc-enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager

Description: Microsoft.SecretSyncController appears to manage the synchronization of secrets between designated resources or systems. Its exact security model and standalone service association are not clearly documented.

Microsoft Security Copilot uses generative AI to assist security operations, investigation, and threat response. This resource provider supports Security Copilot-related management and service integration.

Microsoft.SentinelPlatformServices provides platform resources associated with Microsoft Sentinel security operations capabilities. Sentinel brings analytics, incident investigation, and response automation together for security teams.

Azure Serial Console provides text-based troubleshooting access to eligible Azure virtual machines. Administrators use it to recover or diagnose machines when normal network-based access is unavailable.

Azure Service Connector simplifies connecting Azure-hosted applications to supported backing services. It helps configure connection information, authentication, and permissions for common service integrations.

Microsoft.ServicesHub relates to enterprise Microsoft support experiences, service resources, and administrative integration. It is not generally a resource provider for deploying application infrastructure.

Azure SignalR Service adds managed real-time messaging infrastructure to web and mobile applications. It handles large numbers of live client connections for notifications, collaboration, and interactive features.
Microsoft.SoftwarePlan manages software plan and licensing-related resources used by Azure offers. It supports subscription or license administration rather than hosting a standalone workload.
Microsoft.Solutions provides resources for deploying and managing packaged Azure managed applications. Publishers can offer governed solutions that customers deploy with delegated management options.

Microsoft.Sovereign relates to sovereign-cloud configurations and policies designed around data residency and control requirements. It helps regulated organizations apply sovereignty-oriented governance patterns to Azure.

Microsoft.SqlVirtualMachine manages SQL Server virtual-machine resources and related configuration and licensing integration. It adds SQL-specific management to SQL Server instances running on Azure VMs.
Associated Azure Service: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

Description: Azure Standby Pools maintains preprovisioned compute capacity for selected virtual-machine and scale-set workloads. It helps reduce provisioning latency when applications need new instances quickly.
Microsoft.StorageDiscovery relates to discovering or analyzing storage estates and inventory. Its exact independently marketed scope is not clearly established.

Azure Storage Mover orchestrates migration of files from on-premises sources into Azure storage. It provides managed transfer jobs and progress monitoring for supported source and target combinations.
Azure File Sync synchronizes Windows Server file shares with Azure Files. It enables cloud tiering, centralized file storage, and hybrid file-server scenarios.

Microsoft.SupercomputerInfrastructure represents specialized high-performance or AI supercomputing infrastructure management. It is not documented as a standard self-service Azure compute product for general customers.

Microsoft.SustainabilityServices provides resources related to sustainability or environmental measurement workflows. It is associated with Microsoft cloud sustainability capabilities rather than a general cloud-compute platform.

Microsoft.Syntex relates to Microsoft Syntex content processing and document intelligence capabilities. It helps classify, extract, and process information from documents in Microsoft 365-oriented workflows.
Microsoft.ToolchainOrchestrator appears to coordinate development or infrastructure toolchain resources. A specific public-facing Azure service corresponding to this provider could not be verified.
Microsoft.UsageBilling manages usage-related billing operations or metadata. It is primarily a commerce platform provider rather than a service customers deploy to run business applications.
Microsoft.Validate appears to provide validation operations for certain Azure management workflows. No independently documented Azure service can be confidently assigned to this namespace.

Azure AI Video Indexer analyzes video and audio to produce searchable insights such as transcripts, detected entities, and visual metadata. It helps applications enrich and index media content using AI.

Microsoft.VMware is a resource provider associated with VMware-based solutions on Azure. It is listed by Microsoft in the Azure VMware Solution family, which hosts VMware private-cloud workloads on Azure infrastructure.

Microsoft.WeightsAndBiases supports the Weights & Biases partner offering for tracking experiments and managing AI development workflows. It helps teams visualize model-training runs, datasets, and evaluation results.
Microsoft.Windows365 manages Windows 365 Cloud PC-related resources and integrations. Windows 365 provides persistent cloud-hosted Windows desktops that users can access from supported devices.
Microsoft.WorkloadBuilder appears to support defining or assembling workload deployments and related configurations. It is not documented clearly as an independent Azure service.

Microsoft.Workloads is associated with workload-specific Azure deployment and management resources, including selected SAP-oriented scenarios. It supports managing packaged enterprise workloads through Azure control-plane operations.

Microsoft.ZeroTrustSegmentation is associated with network or workload segmentation aligned to Zero Trust principles. The exact public features and product branding represented by this provider require resource-type-specific verification.

Azure Elastic SAN offers managed block storage for storage-intensive workloads that need scalable storage area network capabilities. It can provide shared storage volumes accessed from Azure virtual machines.

Microsoft.NetworkFunction provides resources for managing network-function instances in supported Azure hybrid or telecom environments. It is associated with deploying and operating network appliances or virtualized network functions.
MongoDB Atlas is a managed MongoDB database offering available through Azure partner integrations. It provides database hosting, scaling, and operational tooling for document-oriented applications.
Napster.CompanionAPI represents a third-party API offering that can be provisioned or managed in Azure. Its exact consumer-facing functionality depends on the Napster product and marketplace terms.
New Relic Observability provides partner monitoring for Azure applications and infrastructure. It collects and correlates telemetry for application performance, logs, and troubleshooting.
NGINX.NGINXPLUS is associated with managed NGINX application delivery and traffic management on Azure. It supports load balancing, reverse proxy, and web traffic control using NGINX technology.

Oracle.Database represents Oracle's database services offered within Azure through an integrated Oracle and Microsoft experience. It enables eligible Oracle database workloads to run in Azure with access to surrounding Azure services.
Palo Alto Networks Cloud NGFW provides a managed next-generation firewall offering integrated with Azure. It helps protect network traffic using advanced inspection and policy-based controls.
Associated Azure Service: Palo Alto Networks Cloud NGFW for Azure

Description: Pinecone VectorDb is a partner-managed vector database offering for AI search and retrieval workloads. It stores and queries vector embeddings to support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation.

Everpure Cloud Azure Native, previously branded under Pure Storage, provides managed enterprise block storage within Azure. It supports storage for selected Azure virtual-machine and Azure VMware Solution workloads with independent scaling of storage and compute.
Associated Azure Service: Everpure Cloud Azure Native (formerly Pure Storage)

Description: Azure Native Qumulo provides a managed scalable file system directly integrated with Azure management and billing. It supports multiple file protocols and distributed unstructured data workloads without customers maintaining the underlying storage infrastructure.
Associated Azure Service: Azure Native Qumulo Scalable File Service

Description: Azure VM Image Builder automates the creation, customization, and distribution of virtual-machine images. It helps standardize VM configurations and keep golden images updated for deployments.
Microsoft.VisualStudio is associated with Visual Studio and historic Azure DevOps account resources. Azure DevOps supports source control, build pipelines, work tracking, and deployment workflows.

Azure HorizonDB is a managed PostgreSQL-compatible database platform designed for scalable, AI-ready transactional applications. It combines separated compute and storage with high availability and native support for vector-based use cases.
